s: a café in a Grade II-listed 1904 Edwardian public convenience
w: A café built into a 1904 Edwardian public toilet block on the corner of Park Row and Woodland Road, closed to the public in 2001 and later given Grade II listing. White tiled walls, a monochrome chessboard floor, marble sinks and oak panelling all survive intact -- even a couple of the original cubicles -- around specialty coffee, homemade cakes and fresh juice.
_facts: Located at the corner of Park Row and Woodland Road, Bristol BS8 1US
Building constructed in 1904 as an Edwardian public convenience, Grade II listed
Public toilets closed in 2001; later converted into a café retaining original tiling, floor and fittings
Some original toilet cubicles preserved as a feature

s: artisan coffee, craft beer and swing seats on St Nicholas Street
w: A coffee shop and bar on St Nicholas Street that gives away its personality through the window -- a pair of swing seats set around a small table at the back. Artisan coffee by day, craft beer and cocktails by evening, plus more than 150 board games on hand, in a space built entirely around not taking itself too seriously.
_facts: Located at 45 St Nicholas St, Bristol BS1 1TP, Old City
Known for swing-seat table seating at the back of the venue
Serves specialty coffee, craft beer and cocktails
Offers a large board game collection for customers

s: the Stokes Croft bakery-café locals queue for
w: A bakery and café on Stokes Croft turning out fresh pastries, good coffee and a hearty brunch menu that keeps a loyal queue moving most mornings. Part of the creative, street-art-lined stretch of Stokes Croft rather than a polished city-centre chain -- one of several Pinkmans locations across Bristol, but the one most tied to the neighbourhood's independent identity.
_facts: Located at Unit 1 Avonmead, 40-48 Stokes Croft, Bristol BS1 3QD
Bakery and café known for pastries, bread and brunch
One of several Pinkmans locations across Bristol
Sits on Stokes Croft, Bristol's street-art and independent-business corridor

s: an old-school independent café institution just round the corner from Stokes Croft
w: A colourful, laid-back Montpelier café on Picton Street, just off Stokes Croft, that's kept its old-school independent character for years -- hearty breakfasts, lunches and a wall of cake options, with a covered patio spilling onto the street that fills up fast on a sunny day.
_facts: Located at 2 Picton Street, Montpelier, Bristol BS6 5QA
Long-running independent café known for breakfasts, lunches and cakes
Has a covered outdoor patio seating area on Picton Street
A short walk from Stokes Croft
